transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I’ve been feeling wound up and on edge for months, like my mood is stuck on high and I’m snapping at everyone, even my own family. It's just gotten to the point where I can't seem to calm down, and my family finally insisted that I come in to get some help.

Can you tell me more about what you mean by feeling 'wound up and on edge' - are you experiencing any physical symptoms like tremors, palpitations, or difficulty sleeping, or is it more about feeling emotionally overwhelmed and irritable?

It’s really a mix of both, but the lack of sleep and the irritability are just awful. I only sleep about two or three hours a night because my mind is racing, and instead of feeling tired, I get up to clean or text people. Emotionally, I feel like I'm on high voltage and end up snapping and yelling at everyone over the smallest things before I can even stop myself.
Have you been experiencing any feelings of extreme happiness, euphoria, or like you're on top of the world, or have grand ideas about yourself or your abilities during this time?

Sometimes I do feel super amped up and invincible, like I'm running on high voltage. I honestly feel like I am meant to do something really big, which is why I think the people at my work and church are trying to set me up to get fired because they're scared of me.

Can you tell me more about what you mean by people being 'scared of you' and trying to get you fired - do you really believe they're plotting against you, or is that just a feeling you have when you're upset?

No, it's not just a feeling when I'm upset—I know for a fact they are plotting against me. The folks at the warehouse and church are constantly watching me and trying to set me up to get fired. They are doing it because they know I am meant to do something big, and they are absolutely terrified of that.
Can you describe a specific situation where you felt like someone was watching you or plotting against you, and how that made you feel and react?

At the warehouse, I'll catch coworkers whispering and moving my pallets around to make me look bad, and at church, people give me these fake smiles while watching my every move. It makes me feel so defensive and tense that I end up snapping at them and demanding to know what they're planning, which just makes them look at me like I'm the one with the problem. I can just feel the threat hanging over me every single shift.
Can you tell me more about what you think is the 'something big' that you're meant to do, and why you believe others are threatened by it?

I'm not completely sure of all the details yet, but I know it's a major purpose, like I'm meant to step up and save people or lead something important. They can sense that power in me, and it scares them because it threatens the way they've always done things. They want to keep me down and get me fired before I can actually make it happen.

Can you help me understand how your feelings of being meant for something big and being plotted against by others are connected, and do you ever have moments where you doubt these beliefs or feel like they might not be entirely real?

I know it sounds crazy to other people when I say it out loud, but I don't really have any doubt that it's happening. The connection is clear to me because they only started plotting and trying to get me fired once I realized I was meant for something bigger. It's like they can sense my potential, and their constant watching and setup attempts are their way of trying to stop me.

Can you tell me if there have been any periods in the past where you felt completely normal, without these feelings of being watched or destined for something big, and if so, how long those periods lasted?

I haven't really had any periods of feeling completely normal lately, as this whole struggle has been building for close to a year. Even when my mood briefly flattened out and I felt totally drained a couple of months ago, the voices and the feeling that everyone was watching and testing me never let up. Those thoughts and the voices have been going strong without any break for at least the last eight months.
You mentioned voices, can you tell me more about what these voices say and when you hear them?

I hear these voices pretty much every day, especially at night or when I'm alone in the warehouse break room. They argue about me, saying I'm a disappointment or that I need to "step up and save people." I hear them clear as day even when there's nobody around and no radio is playing.
Can you describe the voices you hear in more detail, such as how many there are, if they are male or female, and if they ever tell you to do specific things or if they're just commenting on you?

It's usually a couple of voices arguing back and forth, and I hear them clear as day when I'm alone in the break room or at night. They don't really tell me to do specific things, but they argue about me, calling me a disappointment and saying I need to "step up and save people."
Do you ever feel like the voices you hear or the plots you believe are happening are not real, or are you completely convinced that they are real and actually happening to you?

I know it sounds crazy to other people, but I am completely convinced that they are real. I hear the voices clear as day, and I am absolutely sure the people at work and church are plotting against me because they are scared of my potential.
Can you tell me if you've ever had a period where the voices stopped or the plots against you seemed to cease, even if it was just for a short while, and what was happening during that time?

No, they haven't stopped or ceased at all; they've been going strong for about eight months now. Even a couple of months ago when my mood crashed and I felt completely flat and drained instead of amped up, the voices and the feeling of being watched and tested still never let up. They just keep going, no matter how my mood changes.
Can you describe a situation where the voices you hear directly influenced your behavior or actions, and how that made you feel?

When I'm alone in the break room and hear them arguing, calling me a disappointment and telling me to "step up," it puts so much pressure on me. It makes me feel incredibly anxious and wound up, so I start pacing around, talking back to them, or frantically signing up for extra shifts and church events to prove I can do something big. It just leaves me feeling completely overwhelmed and running on high voltage.
Can you tell me if you've ever experienced any periods where you felt like you were in a different reality or had special powers, in addition to the voices and plots you've described?

I don't think I have magic powers or anything like that, but I do know I'm meant for something very big and important. That's why the voices keep telling me to "step up and save people," and why everyone at work and church is plotting against me. They can sense my potential, and they are terrified of what I am meant to do.

Can you help me understand if the voices you hear and the plots you believe in are present all the time, or if they tend to come and go depending on your mood, such as when you're feeling more anxious or 'amped up'?

The voices and the feeling of being plotted against definitely started and were loudest when I was feeling super amped up and wired. But a couple of months ago, when my mood completely crashed and I felt totally flat and drained, they didn't stop at all. The voices and the feeling of being watched just kept going strong for weeks, even though I wasn't feeling high or anxious anymore.
Have you ever had any moments where you questioned the reality of the voices or the plots against you, or have you always been completely convinced of their reality?

I know it sounds crazy to other people, but I've always been completely convinced that they are real. I hear the voices clear as day, and I am absolutely sure the people at the warehouse and church are watching me and trying to set me up because they are scared of my potential.

Can you describe how your beliefs about being meant for something big and being plotted against have influenced your daily life and decisions, and have you noticed any changes in these beliefs over time?

These beliefs have completely messed up my life, making me so defensive and paranoid at work and church that I'm constantly snapping at people. Because of this, I've been written up at the warehouse for not finishing my tasks, and my husband is seriously talking about us separating. The thoughts have been going strong for about eight months now, and even when my mood crashed a couple of months ago and I felt totally flat and drained, the feeling of being watched and plotted against never let up.
Can you tell me if you've ever had any periods where the voices stopped or you didn't feel like you were being plotted against, and if so, what triggered those changes?

No, they haven't stopped at all; they have been going strong and constant for about eight months now. Even a couple of months ago when my mood crashed and I felt flat and drained instead of wired, the voices and the feeling of people plotting against me still didn't let up.
Can you tell me if the voices you hear and the plots you believe in are still present when you're in a calm and relaxed state, or do they only occur when you're feeling anxious or 'amped up'?

Yes, they definitely still happen even when I'm not feeling amped up or anxious at all. A couple of months ago, when my mood crashed and I felt completely flat and drained rather than wired, the voices and the feeling of being watched and plotted against didn't let up at all during those weeks. They are always there, no matter how calm I might try to be.
Have you ever had a period where you didn't have these voices or feelings of being plotted against, and if so, what was different about that time compared to now?

Yes, before about eight to ten months ago, I didn't hear any voices or feel like people were plotting against me at all. Back then, my life was much more normal and stable, even though my husband and I were just starting to have some arguments about money. Now, everything is completely different because I feel constantly wound up, paranoid, and hear these voices regularly.
Can you tell me if you've ever had any moments where you felt like the voices or the plots against you were not real, or have you always been completely convinced of their reality?

I know it sounds crazy to other people when I say it out loud, but to me, they have always felt completely, 100% real. I haven't ever really doubted them because the voices are so clear and the things happening at work and church are so obvious to me.

Can you tell me if you've ever had any experiences where the voices you hear or the plots you believe in seemed to be triggered by anything specific, such as stress, sleep deprivation, or the use of any substances?

The voices and the suspicious feelings definitely kicked in and got much worse when the stress from the money fights and marital tension escalated. They are especially loud and intense when I'm barely sleeping only two or three hours a night and my mind is completely amped up. Also, I don't use any drugs or alcohol, so I know it's not from that.

Can you tell me if you've ever had any periods where the voices stopped or you didn't feel like you were being plotted against, and if so, what was different about that time compared to now, and did anything trigger their return?

No, they haven't stopped at all since they first started about eight months ago. Even a couple of months ago when my mood crashed and I felt completely flat and drained rather than amped up, the voices and the paranoid feelings persisted without letting up.

Can you tell me if the voices you hear and the plots you believe in are still as prominent and distressing when you're in a different environment or with different people, or if they seem to be triggered by specific situations or relationships?

The plots are specifically tied to the people at my warehouse and church, as I'm certain they are trying to set me up to get fired. The voices happen pretty much every day, but they are definitely most prominent and hard to ignore when I'm alone, like in the break room at work or at night when I'm trying to sleep.

Can you tell me if you've ever had any experiences where the voices you hear seem to be responding to your thoughts or actions, or if they seem to be completely independent of what you're doing or thinking?

I'm not entirely sure if they are directly responding to my thoughts or what I'm doing. They usually just start arguing about me or telling me to "step up" on their own, especially when I'm alone in the break room or at night.
Can you tell me if you have ever had any periods where you felt like the voices or plots against you were part of a larger, organized plan, or if they seem more like separate, unrelated events?

Yes, I am absolutely sure it is all part of a larger plan. The people at the warehouse and my church are all in on it together to set me up and get me fired because they are scared of the big things I am meant to do. The voices I hear fit right into this too, constantly telling me that I need to step up and save people.

Have you ever experienced a time when your beliefs about being meant for something big and being plotted against seemed to lessen or disappear, even if only for a short time, and what do you think triggered that change?

No, those beliefs and the feeling of being plotted against have never lessened or gone away at all. They’ve been going strong and constant for at least the last eight months now. Even a couple of months ago when my mood crashed and I felt completely flat and drained, the feeling that they were watching and testing me never stopped.
Have you ever experienced any other types of hallucinations, such as seeing things that aren't there, in addition to the voices you hear?
No, I have never seen things that aren't there. I only hear the voices arguing about me and telling me to step up, but it is strictly just sound.
Can you tell me more about what specifically makes you believe you are meant for something big, and how that relates to the plots you think are against you?

I just feel it deep down inside me, like a calling or a major purpose that I'm meant to step up and save people or lead something important. Because I have this great potential, the people at the warehouse and my church are jealous and terrified of what I might do. That's why they are watching me so closely and trying to set me up to get fired, so they can stop me before I even start.
Can you describe a situation where your delusional beliefs and hallucinations directly influenced a significant decision or action you took, and how did that turn out?

Hearing the voices telling me to "step up and save people" and believing I was meant for something big made me make some really rash decisions, like starting new church groups and donating a bunch of money we didn't have. It turned out absolutely terrible because I blew through our family savings, got written up at the warehouse for neglecting my actual job duties, and now my husband is seriously talking about us separating. It's just left me feeling completely ruined and overwhelmed.

inference_history.note: The patient's symptoms of hearing voices, feeling plotted against, and having delusions of grandeur (believing they are meant for something big) are consistent with psychotic symptoms. The presence of these symptoms, combined with the patient's disorganized thinking and behavior, suggests a psychotic disorder. The patient's mood symptoms, such as feeling 'wound up and on edge' and having periods of irritability, could be part of a psychotic disorder or a separate mood disorder. However, the patient's primary symptoms are psychotic in nature, which is why F20.0 and F23 are the current candidates. F25.0 is less likely given the prominent psychotic symptoms and the lack of clear evidence for a manic episode. The patient's symptoms have been persistent for at least eight months, which suggests a chronic course. The presence of delusions and hallucinations, as well as disorganized thinking and behavior, are key features of F20.0. F23 is also a possibility, given the patient's psychotic symptoms and the absence of a clear manic or depressive episode. However, the patient's symptoms do not appear to be brief or transient, which is a key feature of F23. Further evaluation is needed to determine the best course of treatment and to rule out other potential diagnoses.

inference_history.note: The patient's symptoms of hearing voices, feeling plotted against, and having grandiose beliefs about being meant for something big have been consistent throughout the interview. The presence of hallucinations (hearing voices) and delusional thoughts (plots against them, being meant for something big) are key features. While the initial candidates were F20.0 and F23, the patient's description of mood swings, from feeling 'amped up' to crashing and feeling flat, and the impact of these beliefs on their daily life and relationships, suggest the possibility of a mood disorder component. However, the prominent and persistent nature of the delusions and hallucinations point more towards a psychotic disorder. F25.0 is considered due to the presence of prominent psychotic symptoms (hallucinations and delusions) without clear evidence of a full manic or depressive episode as seen in bipolar disorder, but the mood instability and the content of the delusions (grandiose) also keep F23 (brief psychotic disorder is less likely given the duration) and F20.0 (schizophrenia, given the chronic nature of the symptoms and the presence of hallucinations and delusions) in consideration. The patient's conviction in the reality of their delusions and the absence of doubt also supports the consideration of a psychotic disorder.
